On a CB_RECALL the callback service thread flushes the inode using
filemap_flush prior to scheduling the state manager thread to return the
delegation. When pNFS is used and I/O has not yet gone to the data server
servicing the inode
column2: a LAYOUTGET can preceed the I/O. Unlike the async

column1: filemap_flush call
column2: the LAYOUTGET must proceed to completion.

column1: If the state manager starts to recover data while the inode flush is sending
the LAYOUTGET
column2: a deadlock occurs as the callback service thread holds the

column1: single callback session slot until the flushing is done which blocks the state
manager thread
column2: and the state manager thread has set the session draining bit

column1: which puts the inode flush LAYOUTGET RPC to sleep on the forechannel slot
table waitq.
Separate the draining of the back channel from the draining of the fore channel
by moving the NFS4_SESSION_DRAINING bit from session scope into the fore
and back slot tables.  Drain the back channel first allowing the LAYOUTGET
call to proceed (and fail) so the callback service thread frees the callback
slot. Then proceed with draining the forechannel.
